items.title: Here’s the official list of mayoral candidates in the 2026 Mississauga municipal election
items.summary: Mississauga’s mayoral race is heating up with a total of 14 registered candidates vying for the City’s top job in the 2026 municipal election. Voters will head to the polls on Oct. 26 to decide the fate of incumbent Mayor Carolyn Parrish, who was elected during a 2024 byelection after serving as a city councillor and Liberal MP for decades. The latest polling from Liaison Strategies published on Aug. 14 suggests that it is a head-to-head race between Parrish and former Mississauga mayor Bonnie Crombie. Crombie held the position for a decade but resigned in 2024 to lead the Ontario Liberal Party. She later stepped down from that position as well after failing to secure a seat in the provincial legislature during the 2025 Ontario provincial election. She’s now looking to return to her old job in what is expected to be a high-stakes race. Below is the official list of registered mayoral candidates: Parrish is the incumbent Mayor of Mississauga, a position she assumed in 2024. She previously served as city councillor and represented the riding of Mississauga-Erindale as MP. She also served as a trustee and later became the chairperson of the Peel Board of Education. Before public life, she worked as a school teacher in Etobicoke. Crombie was the sixth mayor of Mississauga from 2014 until 2024, when she stepped down to lead the Ontario Liberal Party. She also resigned from that position after failing to secure a seat in the provincial legislature during the 2025 general election.

items.title: Woman arrested after man stabbed in the neck in Mississauga
items.summary: A woman was arrested after a man was stabbed in the neck in Mississauga over the Labour Day weekend. m. on Sunday, Sept. 6, Peel Regional Police said. Officers found a man suffering from a serious stab wound to the neck, police said. He was transported to hospital, where he remains in critical condition, police added. Police said officers arrested a man who was involved in an initial altercation with the victim. Officers later determined the man was not responsible for the stabbing, and he was released, police said. Police identified a woman of interest who had fled the area on foot before police arrival. On Monday, Sept. 7, 42-year-old Lorena Sanchez of Mississauga was located and arrested. Sanchez was charged with attempted murder. She was held in custody pending a bail hearing at the Ontario Court of Justice in Brampton.

items.title: Level up your ride: Back-to-school transit tips
items.summary: Heading to school, college or university? MiWay offers routes, fare options and travel tips for a safe, easy and affordable trip. A new school year means new classes, new schedules, and for many students, new ways of getting around. Back-to-school season is one of the busiest times of the year on the road. To help you travel safely and conveniently, MiWay offers routes to schools across Mississauga, affordable fares and simple ways to make every trip more comfortable. Here’s what you need to know as you start the school year. MiWay routes connect to schools, colleges and universities across the city. Starting September 7, Route 110 University Express runs more often between City Centre Transit Terminal and Clarkson GO Station. As part of this change, Route 110A University Express has been discontinued, with service merging with Route 110 University Express. Regular post-secondary and secondary school service resumes: A new secondary school route, 305 Streetsville SS, has been introduced, operating between Meadowvale Village and Streetsville Secondary School.

items.title: Woman arrested for attempted murder following stabbing in Mississauga
items.summary: A 42-year-old woman has been arrested and charged after a man was stabbed outside a shelter in Mississauga over the weekend. m. in the area of Main Street and Dundas Street East, east of Dixie Road. When officers arrived, they found a man suffering from a serious stab wound to the neck. Paramedics told CP24 they performed life-saving measures before the man was taken to hospital, where he remains in critical condition. Initially, police say they arrested a man who was involved in a altercation with the victim. He has since been released. “As the investigation progressed, officers determined that he was not responsible for the stabbing and he was subsequently released,” police said in a statement. Police then identified 42-year-old Lorena Sanchez of Mississauga as a suspect, who allegedly fled the area prior to police arrival. On Monday, police arrested and charged Sanchez with one count of attempted murder.

items.title: Amherst Father and Son Face Life-Altering Injuries After Highway 403 Chain-Reaction Crash
items.summary: According to WKBW, a father and son from Amherst, New York suffered catastrophic injuries after a chain-reaction crash on Highway 403 in Mississauga on August 11. The outlet reports 43-year-old Masud Biswas and his 12-year-old son Marif had pulled onto the highway shoulder after a minor collision with another vehicle to exchange insurance information, when a third vehicle veered off course and struck the parked car, which then hit both of them. WKBW reports both were taken to trauma centres, and Masud has since had both legs amputated above the knee while recovering at Erie County Medical Center. According to the outlet, Marif, a seventh grader at Amherst Middle School, has undergone multiple surgeries as doctors work to save his legs and remains at Golisano Children's Hospital of Buffalo. WKBW reports the family's neighbor, Matt Higgins, has launched a fundraising campaign to help cover their medical and living expenses while Masud, the family's main income earner, is unable to work.

items.title: Labour Day Toronto and Ontario cities: What’s Open and Closed
items.summary: This year, Labour Day falls on Sept. 7, 2026, in Mississauga, Brampton, Toronto, Hamilton, Oakville, Milton, Burlington, Oshawa, Whitby, Pickering, Clarington, Niagara Falls and the Niagara Region. While government buildings, services and many businesses/stores will be closed on Monday, some places will remain open. However, to avoid disappointment, it’s best to call ahead or check online to confirm if your favourite restaurant or local grocery store is open. Here’s what’s open and closed in southern Ontario towns and cities on Labour Day: Square One Shopping Centre is open, along with Walmart Supercentre, The Rec Room and The Food District. Whole Foods Square One and T&T Supermarket are also open. Residents and visitors can also visit Celebration Square and the Celebration Square fountain, Rabba grocery stores, select Beer Store locations, the YMCA health and fitness centre in Mississauga, restaurants, cafes, and bars that are typically open on Mondays (call ahead to confirm), the Mississauga Chinese Centre, and movie theatres. On Sept. 7, non-emergency federal, provincial, municipal (including City Hall), and Region of Peel offices will be closed. Banks, libraries and some community centres will also be closed. Canada Post will be closed (no mail pickup or delivery), and there will be no waste collection on Labour Day. Garbage and recycling will be picked up one day later than usual, and Community Recycling Centres will also be closed. items.title: Police Call Mississauga Stabbing an Isolated Incident as Search for Second Suspect Continues
items.summary: According to INsauga, Peel Regional Police say the Mississauga stabbing that left one person fighting for their life is believed to be an isolated incident with no ongoing threat to public safety. The outlet reports one suspect was taken into custody at the scene while officers continued searching the surrounding area for a second suspect. INsauga reports police describe the outstanding suspect as a Hispanic woman in her mid-30s, approximately five-foot-four, with blonde and brown hair. According to the outlet, the victim remained in critical condition at a trauma centre as of the latest police update. INsauga reports officers remained in the Main Street and Dundas Street East area as the investigation continued.

items.title: Twin 16-Storey Towers Proposed for Dixie Site Head to Planning Committee
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, city staff are recommending council approve a rezoning application that would bring two 16-storey apartment towers to a 3-acre site at 1225 Dundas Street East in the Dixie neighbourhood. The outlet reports the towers would be connected by a six-storey podium and contain a combined 553 residential rental units, along with ground-floor commercial space. Mississauga.com reports the proposal also includes 34 four-storey back-to-back townhouses, bringing the total to 587 residential units. According to the outlet, the site is owned by a group of five investment companies, including Stephen-Mitchell Realty Limited and Whitehorn Investments Limited. Mississauga.com reports a city staff report noted the property sits within a designated intensification area meant to accommodate significant growth, with Mississauga's planning committee set to vote on the application September 8.

items.title: Mississauga aims to secure over $401M in funding for housing support infrastructure
items.summary: If approved, the funding will support two transit projects including a new Transit Mobility Hub. 4 million from the provincial and federal governments, with that money going toward housing and transit infrastructure. 4 million from the federal and provincial governments to support housing and transit infrastructure, officials announced on Sept. 3. The funding comes through the Development Charges Reduction Program, part of the Canada-Ontario Partnership to Build. The initiative supports municipalities that have reduced development charges to spur housing development, according to a city news release. Mayor Carolyn Parrish, Premier Doug Ford and other government officials made the announcement. Mississauga secured the funds after becoming one of the first Ontario cities to cut development charges by 100 per cent for certain types of housing developments to encourage growth. This reduction remains in effect until March 31, 2029. If approved, the funding will support two major transit projects. , as MiWay’s existing facilities are operating at full capacity, the city said. The city anticipates 50 per cent transit ridership growth by 2035, which would require an additional 250 buses.
